title: Sita calls the forest to witness
hook: carried into the sky, Sita turns the whole forest into witnesses
carry: sakshi: the world is our witness

segments.voice: Yesterday: a holy man at the door, and then a name, Ravana. Sita answered him: the robe doesn't make the sannyasi. The robe doesn't make the sannyasi.

Words didn't stop him. Valmiki says Ravana's face changes, his eyes go red, and the holy man's body falls away like a costume. In its place stands the king of Lanka, huge and dark as a storm cloud. He seizes Sita, and his chariot, waiting out of sight, rises into the sky. Below, the hut gets smaller and smaller. Then Sita does something unexpected. She starts talking to the forest.
screen: `THE COSTUME FALLS AWAY.` → `A CHARIOT RISES.` → `SHE TALKS TO THE FOREST.`

segments.voice: Listen to who she calls. Rama, of course, and Lakshmana, the brother she drove away with cruel words; Valmiki lets that hang. Then everything around her: the flowering trees of Janasthana, the Godavari river, the spirits of the forest, the deer, the birds. Tell Rama that Ravana has taken Sita. It sounds like panic, and partly it is. But it's also a plan. Rama will come back to an empty hut with no one human to explain, so she makes the whole forest her witness. And she names him: not a demon took me, but Ravana. Behind her cry sits an old Hindu idea: nothing is done unseen. The law book of Manu lists the witnesses of every deed, among them the sky, the earth, the waters, the sun, the moon, fire, the wind, the night, and your own heart. Sakshi, the witness. It's why a Hindu couple marries walking around a fire: Agni sakshi, the fire as witness, so the vows are made before a god. Sita, alone in the sky, does the same for a crime. She makes the world testify. Later in the flight, Valmiki pulls the view wide: Sita in yellow silk against Ravana's dark shape, like lightning against a cloud. But first, in a tall tree, she sees a bird she knows: an old vulture, half asleep in the branches. She calls his name.
screen: `THE TREES, THE RIVER, THE DEER.` · `A NAME IN THE MESSAGE: RAVANA.` · `NOTHING IS DONE UNSEEN.` · `AGNI SAKSHI: THE FIRE AS WITNESS.` · then, large: `SAKSHI: THE WORLD IS OUR WITNESS.`

segments.voice: Many Hindus light a small lamp, a diya, at the home shrine. If you can, light one, or a candle, or just turn toward the light from a window. Make one small, true promise for this week, and let the flame be your witness, the way a couple's vows are made before Agni. If you don't pray, simply say it out loud, to the light. Then breathe with it a while.
The abduction. Ravana drops the disguise, and Sita, carried into the sky, turns the forest into witnesses.
Carry this: sakshi, the world is our witness. Up in a tall tree, an old friend wakes. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Ramlila performances stage the abduction, and tellings that follow Valmiki keep Sita's cries to the forest. At a Hindu wedding the couple circles the sacred fire, with Agni as witness (agni sakshi).

fork.setup: your cousin's wedding planner suggests skipping the walk around the fire 'to save time.' what fits today's teaching?
options: keep it: the fire is Agni, the witness to the vows.
skip it; the vows count the same anywhere.
keep it, but only for the photos.
fork.reveal: Hindus make the deepest promises before a witness. the couple walks around Agni so the vows are seen, the way Sita made the world see.

original.note: Sanskrit sītāharaṇa: the carrying-off of Sita. a common name for this episode in tellings and plays.

trapdoor: what you thought: Sita just screams for help.
what it means: she makes the world her witness: the Hindu idea of sakshi, the same reason wedding vows are made before Agni.

what a scholar hears: Aranya 49 has Sita address the trees of Janasthana, the Godavari and the forest beings; Manusmriti 8.86 lists the witnesses of deeds; the lightning-and-cloud image is in Aranya 52.

chat.meaning: Carried off, Sita called the trees, the river and the creatures to witness. Hindus make vows before Agni for the same reason: nothing done is unseen.

Janasthana.meaning: the forest region around Panchavati, once Khara's

Lanka.meaning: Ravana's island kingdom across the sea

Ravana.meaning: the king of Lanka, who carries Sita off
